description: Health providers reported surgical procedures including caesarean sections conducted without anaesthesia and at times without electricity. Aid workers described women undergoing caesareans and emergency operations without sterilisation, anaesthesia or painkillers.

Many mothers are discharged as little as three hours after giving birth because bed numbers collapsed with the hospitals. One account describes a woman discharged after a caesarean without pain medicine, recovering from major surgery in a tent with a newborn.
energy_note: Major surgery, then a tent, the same afternoon.

description: Health authorities report the miscarriage rate rising to nearly 50%, an increase of more than 70% on pre-war averages. In one month the Gaza Health Ministry recorded about 920 miscarriages among roughly 2,000 pregnancies - about 460 per 1,000, against a pre-war average of 140 per 1,000. Nearly 4,000 miscarriages in six months.

A UN report found about 74% of pregnancy losses occurred in the first trimester and 57% of pregnant women were anaemic. Close to half of all births were by caesarean, nearly all for bleeding, hypertension and infection.

aspect: Most receive no prenatal care at all
description: Most pregnant women in Gaza never receive a prenatal checkup, leaving conditions such as preeclampsia undiagnosed - a driver of postpartum haemorrhage, the leading cause of maternal death.
energy_note: The thing that kills you, undetected because nobody looked.

aspect: It did not stop with the ceasefire
description: Doctors report the pattern continuing after the ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, because the causes are displacement, destroyed homes, collapsed primary care and living in tents without running water - none of which a ceasefire repairs.
energy_note: The shooting stopped and the miscarriages did not.
